method.normalization: Unicode NFKC; lowercase; replace Unicode punctuation/symbols with spaces; collapse whitespace; tokenize on whitespace.
method.wer: Word-level Levenshtein distance (substitutions + deletions + insertions) / reference word count. Corpus WER uses pooled word counts, not average clip WER.
method.alignmentTieBreak: Prefer matching diagonal; then substitution, deletion, insertion.
method.median: Sorted observations; arithmetic mean of two middle values for even n.
method.p95: Nearest-rank empirical percentile: sorted[ceil(0.95*n)-1]. For n=6 this is the maximum and is not a stable tail estimate.
method.latency: Existing totalPrepareLoadDecodeMs combines preparation, model loading and decoding. Components cannot be separately attributed. One observation per fixed clip, no repeated-trial inference.

sampledProcessPss.limits: Sampled target-process PSS can miss transient peaks. Not absolute peak, whole UI pipeline/device memory, phone RAM suitability, or battery evidence.

limits: No microphone/capture or Android recognizer accuracy measured.
Each request loads/frees its decoder; warm disk/page caches may remain.
Sampled process PSS is not absolute peak, whole UI pipeline memory or phone battery.
Synthetic English SAPI voice is not Filipino-accented speech or a noise study.
No scheduling command executes; hypotheses are synthetic benchmark output only.
Only six fixed synthetic English clips from one installed Windows SAPI voice; normalized exact matches are not a human-speech accuracy estimate.
No ACK or snooze utterance exists in this corpus. The today clip can test visible capture/ambiguous fallback only; it cannot establish ACK/snooze recognition.
Direct PCM decoding bypasses microphone/AudioRecord capture, Android platform recognizer and reminder interaction. No scheduling side effects execute.
A single x86_64 emulator run with a pre-existing model cache cannot establish physical ARM64, low-memory phone, OEM behavior, battery or audibility results.
No comparison baseline or performance improvement claim is derived.
